name: ARCHIVE the results tree before any --clean-stale
why: Jobs below pass --clean-stale, which DELETES rows whose config differs -- and the livecodebench (n=15) and math500 (n=30) rows for both winners come from the RETIRED M2 Max box. They are NOT re-measurable at any price, so losing them is unrecoverable. Results are gitignored, so git is no safety net. This runs FIRST, every time, and is cheap (~15MB).
cmd: D=$HOME/mlx_bench_snapshots/pre-queue-$(date +%Y-%m-%d-%H%M) && mkdir -p "$D" && cp -a benchmark/results/. "$D"/ && du -sh "$D" && ls "$D" | wc -l

name: gemma-4-31B-it-qat-6bit evalplus n=100 deployed
why: Fills the CODING use case for a third candidate at usable n. Its existing rows are n=10 (+/-40pp) from the retired M2 box at the `production` profile, so they cannot support a use-case pick. Runs at its OWN registry budget (16384) per operator decision D1 -- characterise each candidate at what it CAN do; the scoreboard shows the budget so acc_strict is never read across budgets.
cmd: PYTHONPATH=benchmark .venv-bench/bin/python benchmark/run.py generate --models gemma-4-31B-it-qat-6bit --benches humanevalplus,mbppplus --limit humanevalplus=100,mbppplus=100 --sampling-profile deployed --order model --clean-stale --probe-timeout 3600

name: SMOKE: runaway-tax temperature ladder (Ornith, 3 known runaway ids)
why: CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE ITEM ON THE BOARD, and it goes early per the operator's 'instruct early corrections'. The runaway tax is ~40% of wall-clock on BOTH winners -- larger than everything Phase 2 shipped. Uses --ids to vary ONE knob on EXACTLY the items that ran away, and MLX_BENCH_RESULTS to give each rung its own tree (a shared tree would either clobber the baseline via --clean-stale or skip every item via done_ids). Worst case 3 items x ~10 min per rung; a rung that FIXES the loop drops to ~20s/item, so success is cheap and failure is bounded.
cmd: for T in 0.2 0.6; do MLX_BENCH_RESULTS=$HOME/ladder_t$T PYTHONPATH=benchmark .venv-bench/bin/python benchmark/run.py generate --models Ornith-1.0-35B-mlx-uniform-4bit --benches humanevalplus --limit humanevalplus=100 --ids humanevalplus=HumanEval/94:HumanEval/83:HumanEval/144 --temp $T --sampling-profile deployed --probe-timeout 1200 || true; done

name: SMOKE: BFCL live, tiny
why: BFCL fills an EMPTY use case (tool calling) and is the only POWERED axis the suite owns (0.94 vs 0.749 at n=1000 is ~12 sigma). It has NEVER run live. Its known risk is that the shim posts a pre-formatted prompt to /v1/completions, BYPASSING the chat template that enable_thinking drives -- so a 5-item smoke says in minutes whether the axis is even valid, instead of after hours. Trailing || true so a broken axis does not stall the queue.
cmd: PYTHONPATH=benchmark .venv-bench/bin/python benchmark/run.py generate --models Ornith-1.0-35B-mlx-uniform-4bit --benches bfcl --limit bfcl=5 --sampling-profile deployed --probe-timeout 900 || true

name: gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit evalplus n=100 deployed
why: Fourth candidate on the coding axis. Existing rows are n=3. MoE/4-bit, so it also gives the suite a second architecture class at usable n.
cmd: PYTHONPATH=benchmark .venv-bench/bin/python benchmark/run.py generate --models gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit --benches humanevalplus,mbppplus --limit humanevalplus=100,mbppplus=100 --sampling-profile deployed --order model --clean-stale --probe-timeout 3600

name: ifeval n=200 gemma-4-31B-it-qat-6bit  [~10h measured]
why: The DAILY DRIVER use case has data for only two models. n=200 gives +/-8.9pp, enough to separate a candidate from the two winners' 89.9%. MEASURED COST: gemma runs ~14 tok/s and ifeval items are ~2.4K tokens median, so ~3 min/item => ~10h for 200.
cmd: PYTHONPATH=benchmark .venv-bench/bin/python benchmark/run.py generate --models gemma-4-31B-it-qat-6bit --benches ifeval --limit ifeval=200 --sampling-profile deployed --order model --clean-stale --probe-timeout 3600

name: math500 n=100 both winners  [~35h measured -- REVIEW BEFORE IT RUNS]
why: The REASONING use case is currently UNRESOLVED: at n=30 acc ties (83.3 vs 81.5) while acc_strict splits 60.0 vs 81.5 because Ornith-1.0-35B-mlx-uniform-4bit hits the budget on 9/30. +/-23pp cannot settle a 21pp split; n=100 gives +/-12.5pp. MEASURED COST: 8.3 min (Ornith) + 12.6 min (the other) = ~21 min per item-pair, so n=100 is ~35h of the single worker. My original queue understated this. Consider n=40 (+/-20pp) for ~14h.
cmd: PYTHONPATH=benchmark .venv-bench/bin/python benchmark/run.py generate --models Ornith-1.0-35B-mlx-uniform-4bit,Qwen3.6-27B-Opus-Distill-OptiQ-4bit --benches math500 --limit math500=100 --sampling-profile deployed --order roundrobin --clean-stale --probe-timeout 5400

name: livecodebench n=100 x4  [~55h+ measured -- LIKELY TOO EXPENSIVE AS SPECIFIED]
why: The only coding axis with per-difficulty breakdown. Every existing LCB row is n=15 (+/-32pp) from the retired box at the `official` profile, so the recorded three-way tie at 80% rests on nothing usable. n=100 gives +/-12.5pp. Roundrobin so a stopped prefix stays balanced across models. MEASURED COST: 9.6 min (Ornith) and 23.1 min (the other) per item, so 100 items x 2 winners alone is ~55h before the gemmas. Either cut n to ~30 (+/-23pp), drop to two models, or skip -- the coding use case already has evalplus at n=100.
cmd: PYTHONPATH=benchmark .venv-bench/bin/python benchmark/run.py generate --models Ornith-1.0-35B-mlx-uniform-4bit,Qwen3.6-27B-Opus-Distill-OptiQ-4bit,gemma-4-31B-it-qat-6bit,gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit --benches livecodebench --limit livecodebench=100 --sampling-profile deployed --order roundrobin --clean-stale --probe-timeout 5400

name: grade everything generated so far
why: Mechanical, no worker time. Writes per-pair .score.json files so the scoreboard shows acc/acc_strict for every row above. Runs last so it covers the whole batch. NOTE 2026-08-14: evalplus in docker PRINTS ITS RESULTS AND THEN NEVER EXITS, so subprocess.run waits out our 3600s timeout and a COMPUTED result is discarded as TimeoutExpired while a ~4.5GB container leaks. Expect mbppplus cells to fail until that is fixed.
